elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (b): "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (c) triggers "where HDI processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" — covering every category of Customer data, not selected named types — with "cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000".

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (d): "workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "HDI shall provide certificates of insurance to the Company on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (b) requires E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000, which satisfies the USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (c) requires cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000, which satisfies the USD 2,000,000 floor.

reasons: The rule is correctly classified as missing: the deterministic searches and the read of Sections 1–10 show no insurance covenant, and HDI hosts the Site and handles Company Content and user data, so the absence is walk-away territory.
All six preferred elements are rendered in operative language with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence / aggregate), and party direction (HDI as insured obligor).
The cyber trigger is drafted by reference to "any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company," which covers every category of Customer data rather than selected named data types.

Minimal: the insertion is a single concise paragraph carrying only checklist items; model extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year post-term tail) were correctly omitted, no additional procedures or remedies were added, and no existing language was deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the new paragraph sits in General Provisions after 10.8, introduces no undefined terms or cross-references, and does not contradict any retained allocation, remedy, or commercial mechanic. Only cosmetic point (not a defect): the inserted heading is unnumbered in the rendered text while the comment refers to 10.9 — number it 10.9 for consistency.
